A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TIC-FT research, with matching authors, algorithms, experiments and appendices. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable and support a reliable comparison despite additions and relocation in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation experiments, quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–2, qualitative results, and appendix analyses of training duration and buffer designs.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds quantitative condition-frame and buffer-frame sensitivity results in Table 3.

M1.justification: Temporal concatenation, buffer construction and noise schedules, target-only training loss, and inference updates remain unchanged in Sections 3.1–3.5 and Algorithms 1–2. The added temporal-reasoning characterization does not introduce a new computational component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same datasets and conditional-generation tasks, including DTU object-to-motion, SSv2 action transfer, character generation, style transfer, interpolation and multiple-image conditioning. Table 3 varies configurations within existing I2V coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain ControlNet, Fun-pose and SIC-FT-Replace, together with the same TIC-FT variants. The appendix retains the ControlNet training-time comparison and constant-noise comparators; Table 3 adds parameter sweeps rather than another comparison method.

E3.justification: New Table 3 evaluates condition-frame and buffer-frame counts of 1, 3, 6 and 9, adding Dynamic Degree to the buffer-count evaluation. These are additional evaluation settings; the original benchmark protocols and documented default configuration remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 already includes qualitative buffer-length tests covering one to five frames and noise-schedule ablations. v2 retains these and adds quantitative condition-count and buffer-count analyses, providing limited additional evidence about fidelity and motion tradeoffs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2's checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of statistical uncertainty reporting but adds no estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds numerical results: within its condition-count sweep, CLIP-I rises from 0.8329 to 0.8396; within its buffer-count sweep, Dynamic Degree rises from 0.72 to 0.82 while CLIP-I falls from 0.7864 to 0.7544. Existing benchmark and appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the training objective and mathematical formulation are unchanged. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and the temporal-reasoning wording adds no mathematical definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The title and abstract newly characterize TIC-FT as involving temporal reasoning, and Section 3.3 explicitly attributes that role to buffer frames. This adds a limited mechanism claim; the central claims about few-shot adaptation, flexible conditioning, efficiency and comparative performance remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new frame-count tradeoffs and recommends one condition frame with three buffers. Section 5 more explicitly identifies paired task-specific training and multitask/zero-shot generalization boundaries. The earlier ten-second memory limitation remains in the checklist, although omitted from the revised conclusion.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds stated licenses or usage terms for DTU, SSv2, FLUX, Sora and Wan2.1. The checklist adds code/data release and training-script statements, but the PDFs do not establish actual availability. Existing implementation, hardware and preprocessing details are retained.

R1.justification: The same 38 references and substantive related-work comparisons are retained. The revised conclusion reiterates the distinction between fine-tuning and parameter-free ICL already discussed in v1, without introducing a new prior-work relationship.

P1.justification: v2 edits the title and abstract, adds ablation subheadings, expands Section 5 into conclusion, future directions and limitations paragraphs, and inserts acknowledgments and a conference checklist. Most scientific prose and the appendix narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 3, renumbers the appendix tables, groups Algorithms 1–2 on one page, and relocates/resizes existing figures within the experimental section. The figure content and training-performance plots are unchanged; the revisions primarily adjust placement and spacing.

improvement.justification: Table 3 adds useful quantitative evidence about frame-count tradeoffs, while Section 5 clarifies task-specific adaptation limits and Appendix A.4 improves licensing transparency. These modest gains are limited by incompletely specified sweep controls and absent uncertainty estimates. The additions also do not separately substantiate the new temporal-reasoning characterization.
